focus: Pawn.HealthScale getter postfix and Hediff_Titan.HealthFactor: re-entrancy (BuildStage -> HealthScale), hot-path cost, threading, effects on existing injuries when the factor drops
diffSource: since build 55 (2026-10-10T03:20:33Z), the last reviewed build, from the build log

findings.title: Lowering the health factor can kill a wounded titan on the spot
findings.detail: Injury severity is absolute hit points. GetPartHealth subtracts it from part.def.GetMaxHealth(pawn), which is now hitPoints × HealthScale, and floors only non-destroying injuries at 1. LethalDamageThreshold is 150 × HealthScale. When a trait is removed, TraitsChanged calls pawn.health.Notify_HediffChanged, which runs CheckForStateChange, which runs ShouldBeDead. A titan whose injuries were survivable under the old factor can lose a vital part or cross the lethal threshold and die with no warning. For material titans, closing the settings window after lowering healthPerPoint does the same through SettingsChanged. One change: in TraitsChanged (and in SettingsChanged), read HealthFactor before marking the stage dirty and again after. If the new value is lower, multiply each Hediff_Injury's Severity by new/old before calling Notify_HediffChanged, so every part keeps its health fraction. The corpus is silent here because no scanned mod patches this getter, so the remedy is my opinion; the death path is cited.

findings.title: healthPerPoint slider never reaches flesh titans until a trait changes or the save reloads
findings.detail: HealthFactor recomputes only when cachedStage is rebuilt. WriteSettings calls SettingsChanged on every titan, but SettingsChanged sets stageDirty = true and calls Notify_HediffChanged only inside `if (material != null)`. A flesh titan keeps its old healthFactor and its old HediffSet caches. On reload the new factor applies silently, with no CheckForStateChange, so any death or downing it implies waits for the next hit. Move `stageDirty = true` and the Notify_HediffChanged call outside the material check (keep `materialStage = null` inside it). Together with the finding above, this applies the new factor at once and safely.

findings.title: One trait at a factor of 0 wipes out every other trait's bonus
findings.detail: TraitFactor clamps each trait to Mathf.Max(0f, perPoint) before the factors are multiplied. A drawback with pointCost <= -2 at the slider's 0.5 maximum, or a content mod setting healthScaleFactor 0, makes the whole product 0. MinFactor then floors it at 0.25, whatever the other traits add, and Describe prints 'Health: -100%' for that trait. Clamping each trait to MinFactor instead of 0 keeps the other bonuses meaningful. The example Brittle trait (pointCost -1) is unaffected at the defaults.

findings.title: Every HealthScale read pays a weak-table lookup, plus a hediff-list scan for titans
findings.detail: The postfix runs PeekTitan on every pawn. For titans it also runs hediffs.Contains(t). HealthScale is read once per body part in GetMaxHealth and once per injury for pain and bleeding. That is fine at normal hediff counts. If profiling ever shows it, cache the Pawn on the titan and skip the Contains check when it matches. No corpus mod patches this getter, so nothing to compare against; this is my opinion.

findings.title: BuildStage is protected virtual, so a subclass could re-enter HealthScale
findings.detail: The base BuildStage and TitanMaterialUtility.BuildStage read no pawn stat or health, so there is no recursion today. A content mod that overrides BuildStage and reads, say, a part's health from it would recurse through HealthFactor and the postfix. A one-line warning in the BuildStage doc comment covers it.
